name: Archives Act 2014 , 2014

metadata.summary: The Balochistan Archives Act, 2014 provides for the custody and preservation of public records and archival materials of historical significance within Balochistan. It establishes the Balochistan Archives under the Directorate of Archives and creates an Advisory Board to manage these functions. The Act defines what constitutes a public record, regulates access and export of materials, and prescribes penalties for contraventions.

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Al-Hamd Islamic University at Quetta as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It outlines the university's powers to provide instruction, conduct examinations, award degrees, and manage finances. The legislation creates various governing bodies including the Board of Governors, Academic Council, and specific committees for finance, affiliation, and discipline.

name: Bal Sport Board Act 2009.doc , 2009

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Sports Board Act, 2009
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of a Sports Board in the Province of Balochistan and the matter ancillary thereto
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Balochistan Sports Board to promote sports in the province through committees and funds.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Balochistan Sports Board as a body corporate with perpetual succession to oversee sports development in the province. The Board consists of government officials, nominated members, and public representatives, headed by the Minister Incharge of Sports. It creates various committees at district, city, and tehsil levels to manage local sports activities and registration of associations. The Act also provides for a Fund to finance sports promotion, mandates annual audits by the Auditor General, and empowers the Board to make rules and regulations.

name: Bal Employees’ Efficiency and Discipline Act 2011(S&GAD) , 2011

metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for proceedings against the employees in Government and Corporation service in relation to their efficiency, discipline and accountability.

metadata.one_line: This Act regulates disciplinary proceedings, penalties, and inquiries for government employees in Balochistan regarding efficiency and discipline.
metadata.summary: The Balochistan Employees' Efficiency and Discipline Act, 2011 establishes a legal framework for initiating proceedings against government and corporation service employees concerning their efficiency, discipline, and accountability. It defines specific grounds for penalties, outlines the procedure for inquiries including personal hearings and the appearance of counsel, and designates the Chief Minister or delegated authorities as competent and appellate bodies. The Act applies to current, police, levy force, constabulary, and retired employees, with provisions ensuring that proceedings against retired staff are finalized within two years of retirement.

name: Bal Enquiries and Anti Corruption Act, 2010 , 2010

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Enquiries and Anti-Corruption Establishment in Balochistan to investigate specific corruption offences and misconduct by public servants. It grants the Director General and officers powers of search, arrest, and seizure similar to police officers for preliminary enquiries. The Act also repeals the earlier Balochistan Anti-Corruption Establishment Ordinance, 1961, while saving pending proceedings under the old law.

name: Bal Holy Quran (Printing and Recording) Act 2015 (relogious Affair) , 2015

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Holy Quran (Printing and Recording) Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to ensure publication of the text of the Holy Quran free from errors of printing and recording and proper disposal of damaged or Shaheed copies of the Holy Quran in Balochistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Balochistan, except Tribal Areas
repeals: The Publication of Holy Quran (Elimination of Printing and Recording Errors) Act 1973
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine of not less than twenty thousand rupees, or with both
key_definitions: damaged or Shaheed copy of the Holy Quran
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the printing and recording of the Holy Quran in Balochistan to prevent errors and manage damaged copies.
metadata.summary: The Balochistan Holy Quran (Printing and Recording) Act, 2015 was enacted to ensure the publication of the Holy Quran free from printing and recording errors. It establishes a Quran Board comprising prominent religious scholars to authenticate standard copies and supervise error-free production. The Act regulates publishers and recording companies by mandating registration, prohibiting specific printing processes like lithography, and requiring strict adherence to text accuracy. Furthermore, it provides for the proper disposal of damaged or sub-standard copies and imposes penalties for offences related to textual distortion or negligence.

name: Bal Witness Protection Act IV of 2016 , 2016

name: Baln General Provident Investment Fund Act, 1 of 2007 , 2007

The legislation defines specific offences such as electricity theft and criminal breach of trust, prescribing penalties including imprisonment up to one year or a fine of at least PKR 2.00 million. It establishes monitoring mechanisms through the District Administration and Energy Department to track unauthorized reconnections and requires public awareness campaigns.

metadata.summary: This Act provides a framework for resolving civil and criminal disputes through Alternate Dispute Resolution (ADR) mechanisms like mediation and conciliation. It mandates courts to refer eligible cases to ADR centres within specified timeframes, ensuring inexpensive and expeditious justice. The Act defines key terms such as 'ADR person' and 'settlement', establishes confidentiality obligations, and repeals specific sections of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

The Act also outlines penalties for offenses like counterfeiting, unauthorized excavation, and trafficking, while repealing the earlier Antiquities Act, 1975 applicable to Balochistan.

metadata.summary: The Balochistan Domestic Violence (Prevention and Protection) Act, 2014 establishes a legal framework to protect women, children, and vulnerable persons from domestic violence. The Act creates Protection Committees and appoints Protection Officers to assist aggrieved persons, ensure safe shelter, and facilitate counseling. Proceedings under the Act are governed by the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.

It mandates that hotel owners, lessees, or managers must register with local police stations, verify guest credentials using NADRA systems, check baggage for explosives, and submit daily guest information forms. The Act empowers police officers to inspect records and imposes penalties for non-compliance, aiming to effectively combat crime and counter terrorism.

metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Charitable Funds (Regulation of Collections) Act, 1953. It extends the Act's jurisdiction to the whole of West Pakistan, excluding Tribal Areas. The legislation substitutes several sections of the 1953 Act to replace references to the Commissioner with the Government and defines specific exclusions for donations to individuals and income from religious shrines administered by the Chief Administrator of Auqaf.

name: Civilian Victims of Terrorism (Relief and Rehabilitation) Act 2014 , 2014

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Civilian Victims of Terrorism (Relief and Rehabilitation) Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for institutionalized response to redress the hardships faced by the civilian victims and their families; to provide for timely recognition and assistance for civilian victims of terrorist acts; recognize right of civilian victims to receive state assistance for relief, healthcare and rehabilitation; arrange for adequate funds for such assistance; create an effective mechanism to track, investigate and analyze civilian harm in terrorist act; and to deal with ancillary matters;
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Balochistan except the Tribal Areas
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from 14th May 2013
repeals: The Balochistan Civilian Victim of Terrorism (Relief & Rehabilitation) Ordinance, 2013
metadata.one_line: Establishes a fund and mechanism to provide relief, healthcare, and rehabilitation grants to civilian victims of terrorist acts in Balochistan.
metadata.summary: This Act provides an institutionalized response for the relief and rehabilitation of civilian victims and their families affected by terrorist acts. It establishes a Civilian Victims Fund within the Provincial Consolidated Fund to ensure timely payment of grants for harm caused to bodies or property. The legislation outlines procedures for ascertaining victims, defining eligible harms such as death, injury, and property destruction, and mandates annual reports and audits.

name: Code of Civil Procedure (Balochistan Amendment) Act, 2019 , 2019

metadata.short_title: The Code of Civil Procedure (Balochistan Amendment) Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act No. V of 1908) in its application to the Province of Balochistan.
amends: The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
metadata.one_line: Amends the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 to update terminology, time limits, fees, and appeal procedures in Balochistan.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 as it applies to the Province of Balochistan. It substitutes terms like 'Small Claims' for 'Small Causes', sets a fifteen-day limit for pronouncing judgment, and modifies provisions regarding appeals, reviews, and foreign judgments. The amendments also update fee limits in execution proceedings and remove references to the United Kingdom from sections concerning foreign decrees.

name: Code of Criminal Procedure (West Pakistan Amendment)ACT, 1968 , 1968

metadata.short_title: The Code of Criminal Procedure (West Pakistan Amendment) Act, 1968
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.
amends: The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898
metadata.one_line: Amends the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 by substituting 'Not bailable' for 'Bailable' in Schedule II regarding sections 325 and 435 of the Pakistan Penal Code.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 specifically as it applies to the Province of West Pakistan. It directs that in Schedule II of the Code, against sections 325 and 435 of the Pakistan Penal Code, the word 'Bailable' be substituted with the words 'Not bailable'. The Act was passed by the West Pakistan Assembly on July 2nd, 1968, assented to by the Governor on July 16th, 1968, and published in the Gazette on July 22nd, 1968.

name: Compulsory Education Act 2014 , 2014

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Compulsory Education Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the free & compulsory education in the Province of Balochistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Balochistan except the Tribal Areas
repeals: The Balochistan Primary Education Ordinance, 1962 (West Pakistan Ordinance No. XXIX of 1962)
The Balochistan Compulsory and Free Education Ordinance, 2013 (Ordinance No. II of 2013)
metadata.max_penalty: Imprisonment up to one month or fine up to five hundred rupees plus daily fines, or both.
metadata.one_line: This Act mandates free compulsory education in Balochistan, establishing committees and penalties for non-compliance.
metadata.summary: The Balochistan Compulsory Education Act, 2014 establishes a legal framework to ensure free and compulsory education for children aged five to sixteen years within the province. It creates Parent Teacher School Management Committees to oversee attendance and school operations while defining specific obligations for parents and employers. The Act outlines penalties for failing to send children to school or employing them as laborers, repealing previous ordinances on primary and compulsory education.

name: Consumers Protection Act 2003 , 2003

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Consumer Protection Act, 2003
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for promotion and protection of the interest of consumers.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Balochistan
metadata.max_penalty: fine not exceeding ten thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act promotes consumer interests, establishes councils and courts, and regulates trade practices in Balochistan.
metadata.summary: The Balochistan Consumer Protection Act, 2003 aims to promote fair commercial practices and protect the legitimate interests of consumers within the province. It establishes a Consumers Protection Council and Consumer Courts to provide speedy redressal for consumer complaints. The Act defines key terms such as 'consumer', 'goods', and 'defect', imposes obligations on manufacturers regarding pricing and labeling, and prohibits unfair trade practices like false advertising and hoarding.

name: Defence Housing Authority Quetta Act 2015 , 2015

metadata.short_title: The Defence Housing Authority Quetta Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish the Defence Housing Authority Quetta.
metadata.territorial_extent: specified area of Quetta and other Districts of Balochistan
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect from 28th Feb, 2015
metadata.max_penalty: fine extending to two thousand rupees per day or imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with both
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Defence Housing Authority Quetta to provide housing and development schemes for defence forces in Balochistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Defence Housing Authority Quetta as a body corporate with perpetual succession. The Authority is tasked with providing quality living arrangements, developing land for welfare schemes for martyrs' families and defence personnel, and generating economic activity in Balochistan. It defines the composition of its Governing Body and Executive Board, outlines their powers regarding land acquisition and allotment cancellation, and sets penalties for unauthorized property conversion or contravention of the Act.

name: Food Authority Act, 2014 , 2014

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Food Authority Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the safety and standards of food and for establishment of Balochistan Food Authority.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Balochistan, except Tribal Areas
metadata.commencement: on such date in the different areas of Balochistan and to the extent as Government may specify by notification in the official Gazette
repeals: The Balochistan Pure Food Ordinance 1960 (Ordinance No.VII of 1960)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Balochistan Food Authority to ensure food safety and standards within the province.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Balochistan Food Authority to protect public health by regulating food safety and standards. It defines various terms related to food, including adulterated food and consumers, and sets up a Scientific Panel and food laboratories. The Act outlines the powers of the Authority, licensing requirements for food businesses, and penalties for offences such as selling substandard or misbranded food.

name: Forest West Pakistan Amendment Ordinance 1962 , 1962

metadata.short_title: The Forest (West Pakistan Amendment) Ordinance, 1962
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Forest Act, 1927.
metadata.territorial_extent: the Province of West Pakistan, except the Districts of Dadu, Hyderabad, Tharparkar, Upper Sind Frontier, Larkana, Nawab Shah, Sanghar and Sukkur, [Karachi Division] and the [Tribal Areas]
amends: The Forest Act, 1927
metadata.one_line: Amends the Forest Act, 1927 in West Pakistan by substituting 'vehicles' for 'carts'.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Forest Act, 1927 specifically for its application to certain parts of the Province of West Pakistan. It substitutes the word 'vehicles' for the word 'carts' wherever it occurs in the Act within the specified districts and areas. The amendment excludes specific districts such as Dadu, Hyderabad, Tharparkar, and others from this substitution. The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of West Pakistan on January 22, 1962.

name: Gawadar University Act, 2018 , 2018

metadata.short_title: The University of Gwadar Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of a University at Gwadar dissemination of knowledge and the matters connected therewith or ancillary thereto.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may appoint and notify in the official Gazette
repeals: The University of Turbat Act, 2012
metadata.one_line: Establishes the University of Gwadar in Balochistan, defining its structure, authorities, and functions.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a new university at Gwadar by upgrading the existing campus of the University of Turbat. It defines the university's constitution, officers, and various governing bodies such as the Senate and Syndicate. The legislation also outlines provisions for affiliated institutions, the university fund, and general administrative procedures.

name: GIEDA Act No. II of 2009 , 2009

metadata.short_title: Gwadar Industrial Estates Development Authority Act, 2009
metadata.long_title: An act to establish the Gwadar Industrial Estates Development Authority (GIEDA).
metadata.territorial_extent: Tehsils Gwadar, Pasni, Jiwani and Ormara of District Gwadar, and to such other areas as the Government may by notification in the Official Gazette notify.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Gwadar Industrial Estates Development Authority to promote and develop industrial estates in District Gwadar.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Gwadar Industrial Estates Development Authority (GIEDA) as a body corporate for the promotion and development of industrial estates in District Gwadar, Balochistan. The Authority is managed by a Board of Directors appointed by the Government, with a Managing Director serving as the Principal Executive Officer. It outlines the Authority's powers to acquire property, maintain accounts, submit annual reports, and make rules or regulations for its administration.

name: Gwadar Development Authority Act, 2003 , 2003

metadata.short_title: The Gwadar Development Authority Act, 2003
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of an Authority for the planning, development, improvement and construction of Gwadar.
metadata.territorial_extent: the Gwadar Tehsil of Gwadar District and any other areas which the Government may notify from time to time
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Gwadar Development Authority for planning and development in Gwadar District.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Gwadar Development Authority to plan, develop, improve, and construct infrastructure in Gwadar. The Authority is a body corporate with powers to acquire property, manage funds, and make rules or regulations. It defines specific terms related to land, buildings, and governance, and outlines procedures for land acquisition, removal of unauthorized structures, and the use of police assistance.

name: Health Thalassemia Act 2015 , 2015

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Prevention and Control of Thalassemia Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for prevention and control of Thalassemia in Balochistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Balochistan, except Tribal Areas
metadata.max_penalty: rupees one hundred thousand or departmental penalty for negligence
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes a board and sets rules for preventing and controlling Thalassemia in Balochistan through screening and counseling.
metadata.summary: The Act aims to prevent and control Thalassemia in the Province of Balochistan by establishing a dedicated Board and Fund. It mandates pre-marital blood screening, genetic counseling, and antenatal testing for carriers while defining specific medical terms and penalties for negligence. The Government is empowered to make rules and ensure diagnostic facilities are accessible to residents.

name: Hotels and Restaurants Act 2014 , 2014

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Hotels and Restaurants Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide measures for controlling and regulating the standards of service and amenities for tourists in hotels and restaurants in Balochistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Balochistan, except Tribal Areas
repeals: The Pakistan Hotels and Restaurants Ordinance, 1976 (Act No. XXXX of 1976) as applicable to the Province of Balochistan
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates service standards, amenities, licensing, and fair rates for hotels and restaurants in Balochistan.
metadata.summary: The Balochistan Hotels and Restaurants Act, 2014 establishes a regulatory framework to control and regulate service standards and amenities for tourists in the province. It creates specific roles such as a Director, Deputy Director, and an Advisory Committee to oversee administration. The Act mandates registration, classification of hotels by star rating, fixation of fair rates, and provision of medical facilities based on hotel size.

name: Lasbela University of Agriculture, Water and Marine Sciences Act, 2010 , 2010

metadata.short_title: Lasbela University of Agriculture, Water and Marine Sciences Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Lasbela University of Agriculture Water and Marine Sciences and for the matters connect therewith or ancillary thereto.

metadata.one_line: Establishes the Lasbela University of Agriculture, Water and Marine Sciences in Balochistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Lasbela University of Agriculture, Water and Marine Sciences at Uthal to promote knowledge in Balochistan. It defines the university's corporate structure, including the Chancellor, Senate, Syndicate, and Academic Council, and outlines their respective powers and duties. The legislation also provides for the appointment of staff, management of university funds, auditing procedures, and the power to allow government employees to serve within the university.

name: Lasbela University of Agriculture, Water and Marine Sciences Act, 2010 , 2010

metadata.short_title: Lasbela University of Agriculture, Water and Marine Sciences Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Lasbela University of Agriculture Water and Marine Sciences and for the matters connect therewith or ancillary thereto.
repeals: Lasbela University of Agriculture Water and Marine Science Ordinance 2007 (XVI of 2007)
establishes: Lasbela University of Agriculture, Water and Marine Sciences
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Lasbela University of Agriculture, Water and Marine Sciences in Balochistan.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Lasbela University of Agriculture, Water and Marine Sciences at Uthal to promote knowledge advancement in Balochistan. It defines the university's corporate structure, including the Chancellor, Senate, Syndicate, and Academic Council, and outlines their respective powers and duties. The Act also provides for the creation of statutes, regulations, and rules governing the university's administration, finances, and staff appointments.

name: Mines (Amendment) Act, 2011 , 2011

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Mines (Amendment) Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Mines Act 1923 (Act No. IV of 1923).
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Balochistan except the tribal Areas
amends: The Mines Act, 1923 (Act No. IV of 1923)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Mines Act 1923 to increase safety and training fees and raise fines for violations in Balochistan.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Mines Act 1923 to update financial provisions related to mining operations in Balochistan. It substitutes specific duty amounts for safety, rescue, and training fees, changing them from paise or lower rupee amounts to five rupees. Additionally, the Act increases the fines applicable to various violations under sections 36, 39, and 40 of the original Mines Act.

name: Nawab Shaeed Ghous Bakhsh Raisani Memorial Hospital Act 2012 , 2012

metadata.short_title: The Nawab Shaheed Ghous Baksh Raisani Hospital Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act, to provide for the establishment of Nawab Shaheed Ghous Baksh Raisani Memorial Hospital, Mastung for the provisions of modern medical facilities to the people of the area at their door steps at level of tertiary care hospital. Further to become an extended part of existing teaching hospital attached with medical colleges.
establishes: Nawab Shaheed Ghous Baksh Raisani Hospital, Mastung
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Nawab Shaheed Ghous Baksh Raisani Memorial Hospital in Mastung for tertiary care and medical education.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Nawab Shaheed Ghous Baksh Raisani Memorial Hospital in Mastung to provide modern medical facilities at a tertiary care level. It creates a body corporate with perpetual succession to manage the hospital, including its funds, budget, and accounts. The legislation outlines the administration by a Board of Governors, the appointment of officers, and the integration of the facility with existing teaching hospitals for medical education.

name: Prisoners ( Baln Amendment) Act, 2011 , 2011

metadata.short_title: The Prisoners (Balochistan Amendment) Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Prisoners Act, 1900 (Act No. III of 1900).
amends: The Prisoners Act, 1900
metadata.one_line: Amends the Prisoners Act, 1900 regarding prisoner transfers and appeals in Balochistan.
metadata.summary: This Act amends section 29 of the Prisoners Act, 1900 to substitute 'imprisonment for life' for 'transportation'. It introduces requirements for serving notice and providing opportunities to show cause before transferring prisoners within the province or Pakistan. The Act also establishes an independent tribunal for appeals against transfer orders and specifies exceptions where notices are not required.

name: Prohibition of Kite Flying Activities Act 2006 , 2006

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Prohibition of Kite Flying Activities Act, 2006
metadata.long_title: An Act to prohibit the Kite Flying in the Province of Balochistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Balochistan except the Tribal Areas
repeals: The Balochistan Prohibition of Kite Flying Activities Ordinance, 2006 (III of 2006)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years or fine not exceeding one hundred thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: This Act prohibits kite flying in Balochistan to ensure public safety and regulates the sale of kites.
metadata.summary: The Act prohibits kite flying in the Province of Balochistan, specifically banning the use of metallic wires or threads coated with sharp materials that endanger life or property. It empowers the Nazim of a district to allow kite flying for up to fifteen days during the spring season upon government approval but strictly forbids the sale of dangerous materials. The legislation establishes criminal offences with penalties including imprisonment and fines, grants police powers for search and seizure without warrants, and provides for the registration of manufacturers and sellers.

name: Prohibition of Private Money Lending Act, 2014 , 2014

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Prohibition of Private Money Lending Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to prohibit the private money lending in the province of Balochistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Balochistan except Tribal Areas
repeals: The Balochistan Money-Lenders Ordinance 1960 (W.P. Ordinance XXIV of 1960)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years or with fine which may extend to one million rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: Prohibits private money lending in Balochistan and repeals the 1960 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act prohibits private money lending within the Province of Balochistan, excluding Tribal Areas. It defines key terms such as 'Private Money Lender' and 'Interest', and establishes severe penalties including up to ten years imprisonment or a fine of one million rupees for violations. The legislation also repeals the previous Balochistan Money-Lenders Ordinance 1960.

name: Prohibition of Sheesha Smoking in Baln, Act 2016 , 2016

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Prohibition of Sheesha Smoking Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the prohibition of sheesha smoking in Balochistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Balochistan, except the Tribal Areas
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine which may extend to one Hundred thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: This Act prohibits sheesha smoking in Balochistan and prescribes punishments for violations.
metadata.summary: The Balochistan Prohibition of Sheesha Smoking Act, 2016 was enacted to prevent sheesha smoking in the province to save human life. It applies to the whole of Balochistan except the Tribal Areas and defines specific terms related to chemical drugs, flavors, and places where smoking occurs. The Act prohibits manufacturing, selling, purchasing, storing, using, or importing sheesha materials and establishes offences with summary trial procedures.

name: Prosecution Service Act 2003 , 2003

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Prosecution Service (Constitution, Function and Powers) Act, 2003
metadata.long_title: An Act to recognize and establish the Prosecution Service in the Province of Balochistan.
metadata.commencement: on a date notified by the Provincial Government in the official gazette
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Prosecution Service in Balochistan, defining its constitution, functions, powers, and administration.
metadata.summary: This Act recognizes and establishes the Balochistan Prosecution Service within the Province of Balochistan. It outlines the constitution of the service, including the appointment of a Prosecutor General and District Public Prosecutors, and vests administrative control with the Government. The legislation defines the functions of public prosecutors, recruitment procedures through the Public Service Commission, and mechanisms for liaison with police authorities.

name: Protection & Promotion of Breast-Feeding and Child Nutrition Act 2014 , 2014

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Protection and Promotion of Breast-Feeding and Child Nutrition Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for protection of breast-feeding and nutrition for infants and young children
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Province of Balochistan except the Tribal Areas
repeals: Protection of Breast-Feeding and Child Nutrition Ordinance, 2002
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which shall not be less than fifty thousand rupees or more than five hundred thousand rupees, or both
metadata.one_line: This Act protects breast-feeding and child nutrition in Balochistan by regulating designated products and establishing an Infant Feeding Board.
metadata.summary: The Act provides for the protection of breast-feeding and nutrition for infants and young children within the Province of Balochistan. It regulates the marketing and promotion of designated products, including breast milk substitutes and feeding accessories, while prohibiting certain practices. The legislation establishes an Infant Feeding Board to oversee implementation, monitor compliance, and handle investigations into contraventions.

name: Provincial Assembly of Balochistan privileges act 1975 , 1975

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Assembly of Balochistan Privileges Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the privileges of the Provincial Assembly of Balochistan, its Members and Committees.
repeals: Balochistan Act No. VII of 1973
metadata.one_line: Defines privileges, immunities, and procedural rules for members of the Provincial Assembly of Balochistan.
metadata.summary: This Act defines the privileges of the Provincial Assembly of Balochistan, its Members, and Committees. It grants immunity from civil or criminal action for matters brought before the Assembly and restricts the detention of Members during sessions. The legislation also outlines allowances, accommodation rights, and specific procedures for summoning witnesses and inspecting jails.

name: Provincial Employee social security ordinance 1965 , 1965

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Employees Social Security Ordinance, 1965
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to introduce a scheme of Social Security for providing benefits to certain employees or their dependents in the event of sickness, maternity, employment, injury or death and for matters ancillary thereto.
repeals: The Employees' Social Insurance Ordinance, 1962 (XXII of 1962)
metadata.one_line: Establishes a social security scheme for employees in West Pakistan providing benefits for sickness, injury, death, and maternity.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Employees Social Security Institution to provide financial and medical benefits to employees and their dependents. It covers events such as sickness, maternity, employment injury, disablement, and death. The document outlines contribution schemes, benefit entitlements, dispute resolution mechanisms through a Social Security Court, and repeals previous conflicting laws regarding workmen's compensation in the province.

name: Quetta WASA Act 2004 , 2004

metadata.short_title: The Quetta Water and Sanitation Authority Act, 2004
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of Water and Sanitation Authority for Quetta District.

metadata.one_line: Establishes the Quetta Water and Sanitation Authority to manage water supply, sewerage, and sanitation in Quetta District.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Quetta Water and Sanitation Authority as a corporate body with perpetual succession to manage water supply, sewerage, and sanitation in Quetta District. It defines the constitution of the Board, including the Chairman and Managing Director, and outlines their functions, powers, and duties. The Authority is empowered to make regulations, issue licenses, levy charges, acquire land, and impose penalties for offenses related to its operations.

name: Quetta WASA Act, 2004 , 2004

It defines the composition of the Board, outlines the functions of the Authority, and grants powers for licensing, regulation, and land acquisition. The Act also provides for penalties for offenses related to damage to property or disobedience of orders.

name: Rented Buildings (Security) Act, 2015 , 2015

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Restrictions of Rented Buildings (Security) Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide mechanism for monitoring the business of rented buildings in the province of the Balochistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Balochistan except Tribal Areas
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes a mechanism to monitor rented buildings in Balochistan for counter-terrorism and crime prevention.
metadata.summary: The Balochistan Restrictions of Rented Buildings (Security) Act, 2015 provides a legal framework for monitoring rented buildings within the province. It mandates written agreements with verified tenant credentials, including references and attestation by authorized officials. The Act empowers police and levies to inspect premises and requires landlords and managers to maintain records of occupants in hostels. Its primary purpose is to counter terrorism and effectively combat crime by ensuring the identity and background of tenants are verified before occupancy.

name: Safe Blood Authority Act 2004 , 2004

The Authority is responsible for ensuring safety, protection, and promotion of human life by providing comprehensive and quality Blood Transfusion Services. It regulates the operation of public and private blood banks, issues licenses to medical practitioners and facilities, and sets standards for blood products. The Act also outlines penalties for contravention and provides mechanisms for review and rule-making.

name: Shops and Establishments (Security) Act, 2009 , 2009

name: Special Assistants to the Chief Minister Act 2018 , 2018

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 to introduce new provisions regarding the calculation and recovery of litigation costs. It mandates that parties file details of actual costs before final orders and allows courts to award these costs with interest rates notified by the State Bank of Pakistan. The legislation also introduces penalties for seeking adjournments without sufficient cause and establishes special costs for false or vexatious averments, while explicitly exempting the Government from liability under these new cost sections.

The Ordinance defines key terms such as 'milk', 'milch animals', and 'producer', outlines the constitution and functions of the Board, and provides for its audit and dissolution.

It deems the cadre dissolved as of September 30, 1965, and allocates specific members to various departments of the Provincial Government listed in the Schedule. A Tribunal is appointed to adjudicate claims preferred by individuals or representatives of tribes before a specified deadline. The Ordinance also provides for the vacation of possession by those without valid claims and establishes rules regarding offences and the finality of Tribunal orders.

metadata.summary: The Balochistan Prevention of Gambling Ordinance, 1978 was promulgated to re-enact provisions previously under the federal Prevention of Gambling Act, 1977 as a provincial law. It defines common gaming-houses and instruments of gaming while establishing penalties for owning such houses, being found therein, or engaging in public or private gambling. The Ordinance also grants powers to enter and search premises, creates presumptions regarding persons found in gaming houses, and provides for the tender of pardon to accomplices who testify truthfully.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance prohibits the affixing of posters, bills, notices, or writing on walls within the Province of Balochistan (excluding Tribal Areas) with the intention to attract public attention. It defines key terms such as 'cinema house' and 'management', and establishes penalties including fines up to one hundred rupees and arrest without warrant for offenders. The Ordinance also empowers the District Magistrate to exempt specific cinema houses and allows the Government to make rules for its implementation.

metadata.one_line: A provincial policy for sustainable fisheries and aquaculture management in Balochistan from 2025 to 2035.
metadata.summary: This document outlines the vision, mission, and objectives for sustainable fisheries and aquaculture in Balochistan over a ten-year period. It establishes a governance framework involving the Office of the Chief Minister and Coastal Development at Gwadar to manage marine infrastructure and promote public-private partnerships. The policy sets specific targets for stock management, habitat protection, and fishing operations while mandating the alignment or repeal of existing conflicting laws like the Pasni Fisheries Harbour Authority Ordinance, 1983.

name: Government of Balochistan Community Led Local Governance Policy, 2023 , 2023

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Community Led Local Governance Policy, 2023
metadata.administering_body: Local Government and Rural Development Department, Government of Balochistan
metadata.one_line: A policy to empower local communities in Balochistan for socio-economic development and improved local governance.
metadata.summary: The Community Led Local Governance (CLLG) Policy institutionalizes community engagement in local governance within the Province of Balochistan. It aims to reduce poverty, improve public service delivery, and strengthen local government systems by empowering Community Institutions (CIs). The policy outlines a regulatory framework involving legislative, fiscal, and audit requirements, supported by a Policy Implementation Manual (PIM) prepared by the Local Government and Rural Development Department.

name: Government of Balochistan’s Gender Equality & Women’s Empowerment Policy, 2020-2024 , 2024

metadata.short_title: Government of Balochistan's Gender Equality & Women's Empowerment Policy, 2020-2024
metadata.one_line: A policy document endorsed by the Balochistan provincial cabinet to promote gender equality and women's empowerment from 2020 to 2024.
metadata.summary: This policy was developed through a partnership between the Women Development Department, Government of Balochistan, and UN Women Pakistan. It was endorsed by the provincial cabinet on October 8, 2020, with technical support from UN Women Pakistan. The document outlines a vision, mission, and objectives for women's economic, social, political empowerment, access to justice, and climate resilience within the province.

name: Grant in Aid Policy , 2024

metadata.short_title: Grant-in-Aid Policy
metadata.one_line: Policy allocating grant-in-aid funds for minority religious sites, festivals, emergencies, scholarships, and assets in Balochistan.
metadata.summary: This policy outlines the allocation of grant-in-aid funds specifically for minority communities in Balochistan. It designates percentages of funds for repairing religious sites, organizing festivals, providing emergency relief, offering financial assistance for marriage/dowry, funding scholarships, and purchasing physical assets like ambulances. The document establishes a utilization mechanism involving scrutiny committees at provincial and district levels to distribute these funds via cross-cheques to beneficiaries.

name: Pakistan Investment Policy, 2023 , 2023

metadata.short_title: Pakistan Investment Policy, 2023
metadata.one_line: A federal policy to attract high-quality foreign direct investment through incentives and liberalization.
metadata.summary: The Pakistan Investment Policy 2023 aims to transform the economy by attracting high-quality foreign direct investment (FDI) and enhancing economic complexity. It adopts a multi-pronged approach focusing on investment retention, facilitation, and aftercare while targeting sectors that generate jobs and export earnings. The policy provides various incentives including tax exemptions, duty-free imports for machinery, and location-based benefits for under-developed regions and Special Economic Zones (SEZs). Federal BOI and sub-national IPAs are designated to manage incentive applications and ensure investor compliance.

name: The Balochistan Civil Servants Deputation Policy, 2012 , 2012

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Civil Servants' Deputation Policy, 2012
amends: The Balochistan Civil Servants (Appointment, Promotion and Transfer) Rules, 2009
repeals: circular letter No.SORI.1(24)/S&GAD/2007/2334-2453, dated the 21st November, 2007
metadata.one_line: Revises the deputation policy for civil servants in Balochistan, limiting deputation periods to three years.
metadata.summary: This notification revises the deputation policy for civil servants in Balochistan, superseding a 2007 circular. It defines deputation as temporary duty outside a sanctioned appointment and discourages using it for appointments where promotion or transfer rules apply. The policy limits deputation periods to three years with rare extensions and prohibits posting officers to lower posts than their current rank.

name: The Balochistan Civil Servants' Promotion Policy, 2012 (Update-2023) , 2012

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Civil Servants' Promotion Policy, 2012
metadata.one_line: Policy governing promotion, selection, and supersession of civil servants in Balochistan based on merit and seniority.
metadata.summary: This document consolidates the Promotion Policy for Federal Government adopted by the Government of Balochistan with specific additions and omissions. It applies to all civil servants holding regular appointments and establishes criteria for promotion based on seniority-cum-merit or seniority-cum-fitness. The policy defines promotion as advancement to a higher post involving greater responsibility, emphasizing that it is a discretionary executive decision rather than an absolute right. It introduces mechanisms such as the Comprehensive Efficiency Index and outlines procedures for selection boards, supersession, and handling cases where disciplinary proceedings are pending.

name: The Balochistan Civil Servants’ Promotion Policy, 2012 , 2012

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Civil Servants' Promotion Policy, 2012
amends: The Balochistan Civil Servants Act, 1974
Balochistan Civil Servants (Appointment, Promotion and Transfer) Rules, 2009
metadata.one_line: Policy governing promotion, selection, and supersession of regular civil servants in Balochistan based on merit and seniority.
metadata.summary: This document consolidates the Promotion Policy adopted by the Government of Balochistan for all civil servants holding regular appointments. It supplements existing laws by providing comprehensive guidelines on promotion procedures, emphasizing that promotion is a discretionary executive act based on merit, suitability, seniority, competence, and antecedent records rather than an absolute right. The policy establishes criteria for efficiency indices, selection board recommendations, and conditions for supersession or deferment of officers.

name: The Balochistan Digital Policy, 2021 , 2021

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Digital Policy, 2021

Digital Security, Disaster, Rights and Responsibilities
metadata.one_line: A provincial policy to leverage IT for efficient service delivery, economic growth, and digital transformation in Balochistan.
metadata.summary: The Balochistan Digital Policy 2021 outlines the strategic vision of the Government of Balochistan to use information technology for efficient service delivery and economic prosperity. It aims to revolutionize governance through e-Governance, promote e-commerce, and ensure online safety using technologies like AI and cloud computing. The policy details six pillars including digital access, literacy, services, promotion, security, and economy, with specific action plans for short, mid, and long-term transformation.

name: The Balochistan Foreign Debt Management Policy, 2025 , 2025

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Foreign Debt Management Policy, 2025
metadata.one_line: Establishes a framework for managing Balochistan's foreign debt to ensure fiscal discipline and sustainable development.
metadata.summary: The Balochistan Foreign Debt Management Policy, 2025 provides a comprehensive framework to regulate and monitor foreign debt within the province. It aims to ensure that external borrowing aligns with provincial development priorities while maintaining fiscal discipline and transparency. The policy establishes specific committees, including the Debt Management Committee (DMC) and the Foreign Assistance Lead Committee (FALC), to oversee borrowing decisions, project implementation, and audit processes.

It supersedes the existing Balochistan Land Lease Policy 20002 and outlines eligibility criteria, modes of lease, and provisions for taxes and penalties. The policy applies to agricultural, livestock, agro-industrial, educational, residential, and commercial uses of government land within the province.

metadata.summary: This document outlines the Balochistan Provincial Aviation Strategy and a three-year development plan (2025-2028) to promote trade, tourism, and economic growth through the aviation sector. It addresses challenges in local pilot employment by launching a Young Pilot Development Program and aims to establish a self-sustaining provincial aviation maintenance ecosystem. The plan includes phases for infrastructure development, air ambulance services, charter operations, and the formation of an Independent Aviation Advisory Board to oversee implementation.

name: The Balochistan Rangeland Policy-2026 , 2026

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Rangeland Policy, 2026
metadata.one_line: A provincial policy framework for sustainable management and restoration of Balochistan's rangelands.
metadata.summary: The Balochistan Rangeland Policy, 2026 establishes a comprehensive framework to manage the province's vital rangeland ecosystems. It aims to address challenges like overgrazing and climate change while supporting the agro-pastoral economy and biodiversity. The policy promotes community-led governance, sustainable grazing practices, and ecosystem restoration involving local stakeholders.

name: The National Artificial Intelligence Policy, 2025 , 2025

metadata.short_title: The National Artificial Intelligence Policy, 2025

key_definitions: Ministry of Information Technology and Telecom (MoITT)

metadata.summary: The National Artificial Intelligence Policy, 2025 outlines a national strategy to transform Pakistan into a knowledge-based economy through the responsible adoption of AI. It establishes mechanisms such as the National Artificial Intelligence Fund (NAIF) and Centres of Excellence (COE-AI) to foster innovation and research. The policy covers six pillars including innovation ecosystems, workforce readiness, security, infrastructure development, and international collaboration to support digital transformation.

name: The Balochistan Compulsory Teaching of The Holy Quran Act, 2023 , 2023

metadata.summary: The Balochistan Industrial Relations Act, 2022 re-enacts the law governing industrial relations within the province. It aims to conform with international labour standards regarding freedom of association and collective bargaining while fostering trust between employers and workers. The Act establishes mechanisms such as conciliation boards, compulsory arbitration for essential services, and Labour Courts to resolve disputes. It applies to all workers and employers at workplaces within Balochistan but excludes police, levies, defense services, and essential services from certain provisions.

metadata.summary: This notification amends the Balochistan Revenue Department (Subordinate) Service Rules, 1982 regarding Patwari recruitment. It mandates pre-service training through a Patwar Training School/DLR and requires candidates to pass a departmental examination within three chances. Seniority is determined based on merit assigned by the BPSC after training and examination completion. Candidates failing to complete requirements within two years face cancellation of candidature, while those selected via DSC are exempted from certain tests.

The policy mandates that if a suitable candidate is not available in a specific division, the vacancy remains unfilled or is offered to the same division in subsequent years, unless filled via relaxation of zonal quotas.

metadata.one_line: Amends the 1974 Act to allow surplus civil servants to be appointed to equivalent or lower posts with pay protection during reorganization.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Balochistan Civil Servants Act, 1974 to address the absorption of civil servants rendered surplus due to departmental reorganization or abolition of posts. It allows such officers to be appointed to equivalent posts carrying basic pay scales equal to their previous positions, provided they meet applicable qualifications. If no equivalent post is available, they may be offered a lower post with protection for their higher pay until the appointment takes effect. The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of Balochistan under emergency powers because the Provincial Assembly was suspended following the October 1999 Proclamation of Emergency.

metadata.summary: The Baluchistan Civil Servants Act, 1974 establishes the legal framework for appointing persons to civil services within the province. It defines key terms such as 'civil servant', 'probation', and 'permanent post' while setting conditions for tenure, confirmation, and appeals regarding service orders. The Act empowers the Government of Baluchistan to make necessary rules and provides mechanisms for handling difficulties in implementation.

name: The Balochistan Civilian Victims Of Terrorism (Relief And Rehabilitation) Act , 2014

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Civilian Victims of Terrorism (Relief and Rehabilitation) Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for institutionalized response to redress the hardships faced by the civilian victims and their families; to provide for timely recognition and assistance for civilian victims of terrorist acts; recognize right of civilian victims to receive state assistance for relief, healthcare and rehabilitation; arrange for adequate funds for such assistance; create an effective mechanism to track, investigate and analyze civilian harm in terrorist acts; and to deal with ancillary matters.
metadata.territorial_extent: whole of the Province except the Tribal Arcas
metadata.commencement: at once and shall be deemed to have taken effect on and from 14th May 2013
repeals: The Balochistan Civilian Victim of Terrorism (Relief & Rehabilitation) Ordinance, 2013
metadata.one_line: This Act provides relief, rehabilitation grants, and a fund for civilian victims of terrorist acts in Balochistan.
metadata.summary: The Act establishes an institutionalized response to assist civilian victims and their families harmed by terrorist acts. It creates a specific fund within the Provincial Consolidated Fund to pay minimum grants for death, injury, property loss, and livestock damage. The Government is empowered to establish rehabilitation schemes focusing on education, healthcare, and livelihood, while a notified officer handles the ascertainment of victims and communication of details to the Government.

metadata.summary: The Balochistan Compulsory Education Act, 2014 was enacted to provide free and compulsory education in the Province of Balochistan. The Act establishes Parent Teacher School Management Committees to oversee schools, plan schemes like mid-day meals, and monitor attendance. It imposes penalties on parents and employers who fail to ensure child attendance after warnings.

metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to prohibit the expression of matters on walls in the Province of Balochistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Balochistan except Tribal Areas
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine not exceeding Rs. 5,000/- or with both
metadata.one_line: Prohibits expressing matters on walls in Balochistan and imposes penalties for violations.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance prohibits the expression of matters such as posters, bills, notices, or writings on walls within the Province of Balochistan. It applies to the whole province except Tribal Areas and comes into force immediately. The document establishes that anyone affixing advertisements or writing on walls with intent to attract public attention commits an offense punishable by up to six months imprisonment, a fine of Rs. 5,000, or both. Local Councils are mandated to remove prohibited expressions within 30 days of the Ordinance's commencement.

name: The Balochistan Prohibition Of Kite Flying Activities Act , 2006

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Prohibition of Kite Flying Activities Act, 2006
metadata.long_title: An Act to prohibit the Kite Flying Activities in the Province of Balochistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Balochistan except Tribal Areas
repeals: The Balochistan Prohibition of Kite Flying Activities Ordinance, 2006 (III of 2006)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years or to fine not exceeding one hundred thousand rupees or to both
metadata.one_line: This Act prohibits kite flying in Balochistan to ensure public safety and regulates the manufacture and sale of kites.
metadata.summary: The Act prohibits kite flying activities in the Province of Balochistan, excluding Tribal Areas, to protect human life and property. It bans the manufacture, sale, or offering for sale of kites and specific materials like metallic wires or threads coated with sharp substances. The legislation empowers police officers to search, seize, and arrest offenders while mandating registration for manufacturers and sellers. Penalties include imprisonment up to three years or fines up to one hundred thousand rupees for violations.

name: The Balochistan Prohibition Of Private Money Lending Act , 2014

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Prohibition of Private Money Lending Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to prohibit the private money lending in the province of Balochistan.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Balochistan except Tribal Areas
repeals: The Balochistan Money-Lenders Ordinance 1960 (W.P. Ordinance XXIV of 1960)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years or with fine which may extend to one million rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act prohibits private money lending in Balochistan and prescribes severe criminal penalties for violations.
metadata.summary: The Balochistan Prohibition of Private Money Lending Act, 2014 was enacted to prohibit private money lending within the province. It defines a 'Private Money Lender' as an individual who lends money on interest, excluding government banks and cooperatives. The Act imposes strict criminal penalties, including up to ten years imprisonment or a fine of one million rupees, for engaging in prohibited lending activities.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance prohibits the import, manufacture, sale, and use of polythene bags within the Province of Balochistan, excluding Tribal Areas. It applies to factories, shopkeepers, hawkers, and other persons involved in the trade or production of such bags. The law establishes criminal offences for contravention, punishable by imprisonment up to three months, a fine of up to fifty thousand rupees, or both, and classifies these offences as cognizable and bailable.

metadata.summary: The Balochistan Prohibition Ordinance, 1978 was promulgated by the Governor to prohibit the manufacture, sale, and consumption of intoxicating liquors within the province. It defines key terms such as 'intoxicating liquor', 'manufacture', and 'sale' to ensure broad coverage of prohibited activities. The Ordinance establishes penalties including imprisonment and fines for violations and grants powers to Prohibition Officers to enforce these provisions.

name: The Balochistan Prosecution Service (Constitution Functions And Powers) Act , 2003

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Prosecution Service (Constitution Functions And Powers) Act , 2003
metadata.long_title: An Act to reorganize and establish the Prosecution Service in the Province of Balochistan.

metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the Balochistan Prosecution Service and defines its constitution, functions, and powers.
metadata.summary: The Act reorganizes and establishes a separate Prosecution Service for the Province of Balochistan to achieve speedy justice. It creates a hierarchy including a Prosecutor General, District Public Prosecutors, and various Assistant/Deputy prosecutors appointed by the Government. The service is under the control of the Government with administrative functions vested in the Prosecutor General, who distributes work based on jurisdiction. Recruitment is conducted through competitive examinations held by the Balochistan Public Service Commission.

name: The Balochistan Protection of Communal Property of Minorities Act , 2018

metadata.short_title: The Balochistan Protection of Communal Property of Minorities Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to protect the Property of Minority Community of the Province of Balochistan meant for their communal use

metadata.one_line: This Act protects communal property of minority communities in Balochistan by banning its sale or transfer and providing for eviction of illegal occupants.
metadata.summary: The Balochistan Protection of Communal Property of Minorities Act, 2018 was enacted to protect properties meant for the communal use of minority communities in the province. It prohibits any person from buying, selling, or transferring such properties without exception for approved housing schemes. The Act empowers the Government to evict illegal occupants and demolish unauthorized structures, with penalties including up to seven years imprisonment and a fine of at least 100,000 rupees for violations.

metadata.summary: The Act provides a legal framework to monitor rented buildings and hostels in Balochistan to counter terrorism and crime. It mandates written rent agreements with verified tenant credentials, including references and attestation by authorized officials. Landlords and managers must submit tenant information to police within three days of signing an agreement, while private hostels are restricted to enrolled students only. The Act empowers police to inspect premises and imposes penalties for non-compliance or abetment of offenses.

It mandates that authorities must serve a notice to prisoners stating reasons for transfer and provide an opportunity to show cause against it, unless specific exceptions apply such as safety concerns or court requirements. Additionally, it adds a provision stating that death-sentenced prisoners are not treated as condemned until their appeal is dismissed or the sentence is confirmed by the High Court or Federal Shariat Court.

metadata.one_line: This Act prohibits the manufacture, sale, purchase, storage, use, and import of sheesha in Balochistan.
metadata.summary: The Prohibition of Sheesha Smoking in Balochistan Act, 2016 was enacted to prevent sheesha smoking in the province to save human life. It applies to the whole of Balochistan except the Tribal Areas and came into force immediately upon enactment. The Act prohibits any person from manufacturing, selling, purchasing, storing, using, or importing sheesha and related materials like glass hookas and chemical drugs. Offences under this Act are cognizable and bailable, punishable by imprisonment up to three years and/or fines up to one hundred thousand rupees for manufacturers and sellers.
